mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-01.title: Use the average
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-01.body:
The average of the four numbers is $64 \div 4 = 16$, so they are centered on 16: $13, 15, 17, 19$. Product of greatest and least: $13 \times 19 = 247$.

**Answer: 247**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-02.title: Locate the division
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-02.body:
Every expression contains exactly one $\div$, so the result is an integer exactly when that quotient is an integer (the rest is adding/subtracting whole numbers). Integer quotients from distinct numbers: $8 \div 4$, $8 \div 2$, $6 \div 2$, $4 \div 2$ — 4 choices.

The quotient occupies one of 3 positions (first, middle or last pair of blanks). The other 2 numbers fill the other 2 blanks in 2 ways, and $+$, $-$ fill the other 2 boxes in 2 ways.

Total: $4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2 = 48$.

**Answer: 48**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-02.title: Brute-force check
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-02.body:
There are $4! \times 3! = 144$ expressions in all. For the $\div$ in a given position, the pair of numbers around it is an ordered pair of distinct numbers: 12 possible pairs, of which 4 give integers ($8/4, 8/2, 6/2, 4/2$). So exactly $\frac{4}{12} = \frac13$ of the expressions give integers: $144 \div 3 = 48$.

**Answer: 48**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-03.title: List results by quotient
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-03.body:
An integer result needs an integer quotient. The expression then has three terms (the quotient and the two leftover numbers) joined by one $+$ and one $-$, so the result is (sum of the three terms) minus twice the subtracted term, where the subtracted term is any term except the first.
- With $8 \div 4 = 2$ (others 2 and 6): sum 10, results $10 - 4 = 6$ and $10 - 12 = -2$.
- With $8 \div 2 = 4$ (others 4, 6): sum 14, results $6$ and $2$.
- With $6 \div 2 = 3$ (others 4, 8): sum 15, results $9, 7, -1$.
- With $4 \div 2 = 2$ (others 6, 8): sum 16, results $12, 4, 0$.

All integer results: $-2, -1, 0, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12$. Difference: $12 - (-2) = 14$.

**Answer: 14**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-03.title: Aim for extremes
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-30-03.body:
The two other numbers $a, b$ and the quotient $q$ combine as $\pm$ terms with exactly one subtraction. The biggest result adds the two largest and subtracts the smallest: with $q = 4 \div 2 = 2$, $8 + 6 - 2 = 12$ (e.g. $8 + 6 - 4 \div 2$). The smallest subtracts the largest: with $q = 8 \div 4 = 2$, $2 + 2 - 6 = -2$ (e.g. $2 - 6 + 8 \div 4$). Checking the other quotients gives nothing beyond these. Difference: $12 - (-2) = 14$.

**Answer: 14**
